Article Title: 'My phone tapped': Rahul fires salvo at PM Modi; 'get head examined', says BJP
Article Text:
Rahul's charge, fresh debate dare draw sharp BJP response

Akhilesh backs Rahul

BJP hits back

Poll Vote & Share your view Would you like to see a public debate between Rahul Gandhi and PM Modi? Yes, it would be informative No, it's not necessary Only if it is televised Yes, but I prefer it in Parliament 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday accused the Modi government of tapping his phone, claiming that the Prime Minister was aware of the surveillance. He once again challenged PM Modi to a face-to-face public debate, saying it would expose who was under the control of foreign powers and involved in anti-national activities."The Prime Minister is aware of this because he has my phone tapped," Rahul said in a video posted by the Congress on X.Rahul also shared another video on X later, accusing PM Modi of relying on a script and claiming that the pressure of facing him in a debate was getting to the Prime Minister."The stage is yours, the atmosphere is yours—yet you still needed a script. Looks like the pressure got to you," Rahul wrote in the caption.Reiterating his challenge, the Congress leader said, "Anyway, no worries. Bring a teleprompter to a debate with me too, and seat a judge of your choice as well.""Just show up, that’s all. The country wants to know - who is the real traitor?" he added.In the video, Rahul claimed that a direct debate with him could end PM Modi's political career.Rahul said, “I kept repeating it. The Prime Minister's political career, mark my words, the PM's political career will be over if he comes and debates with me.He knows that, and I know that. He keeps calling me anti-national. I want to show the nation exactly who is anti-national, exactly who's controlled by whom and since when. And he knows the truth of that."“Notice something. There's a little fear in his mind because he's no longer commenting on me. He's no longer attacking me. He's been very, very careful. There's a reason for it, guys,” Raebareli MP said.Backing INDIA bloc colleague, Samajwadi Party supremo Akhilesh Yadav said that phones and modern technology could not be trusted in the age of Artificial Intelligence (AI)."One should not trust the technology of today. In the age of AI, anything is possible," Akhilesh said, referring to Rahul's phone-tapping allegation.He also recalled that a leader who was no longer alive had once spoken about his phone being tapped.Meanwhile, the BJP hit back at Rahul's allegations, with Kerala BJP chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar dismissing the phone-tapping claim and launching a personal attack on the Congress leader."Rahul Gandhi, I can only safely say to him, with all respect, must get his head examined. Nobody is bothered tapping his phone. Nobody is interested in tapping his phone. If anybody is interested, it's to understand why his brain only functions on lies day after day," Chandrasekhar said.The BJP had earlier rejected Rahul's demand for a debate with PM Modi. Union home minister Amit Shah had challenged the Congress leader to debate him in Parliament instead, asking Rahul to bring his allegations and arguments to the House rather than take the political debate to the streets.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of tapping his phone, claiming that the Prime Minister was aware of the surveillance. He once again challenged PM Modi to a face-to-face public debate, saying it would expose who was under the control of foreign powers and involved in anti-national activities.

Article Title: 'Don't fall into BJP's trap': Raj Thackeray alleges bid to divide Mumbai over Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Raj Thackeray alleges BJP of 'divide and rule'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena supremo Raj Thackeray on Thursday accused the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai, urging people not to fall in a "political trap."In a post on X, Thackeray alleged that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He claimed that the party and its social media network were circulating reels around Chhath Puja and what he termed cultural aggression to create discord in Maharashtra.Thackeray also referred to Bhojpuri songs being played at some railway stations in Mumbai, claiming that the MNS had intervened to stop the practice."However, the BJP appears to be disappointed that all these efforts have still not managed to create the kind of conflict it expects. And all this exercise is being undertaken with the upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections in mind," he said.Questioning the BJP's political strategy, the MNS chief said the party's think tank appeared to have run out of ideas and that its long-standing "divide and rule" formula would no longer help it win elections.He alleged that the BJP had repeatedly attempted to exploit religious and caste divisions for electoral gains, claiming that it sought to create Hindu-Muslim tensions ahead of Lok Sabha elections and caste-based divisions before state assembly polls."Whenever Lok Sabha elections approach, it tries to ignite Hindu-Muslim tensions. It brings Muslim women wearing burqas into playgrounds and gardens and attempts to scare people by saying, 'Look, look, now they have reached our playgrounds and gardens.' Of course, several videos of people wearing burqas to create an atmosphere of terror among Hindu women and men are already visible on social media," he said.Thackeray also cited the row surrounding Mumbai's Kabutarkhana, alleging that the BJP had attempted to fuel a Gujarati-versus-Marathi divide ahead of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation elections last year."I have said several times in my speeches that when the BJP realises it cannot win elections by showcasing its work, it creates conflict between two groups and wins elections on the bloodshed that follows," he said.He further alleged that the Election Commission played the decisive role in electoral victories, while communal and social conflicts were used by the BJP to explain its success.
Article Summary: Raj Thackeray accuses BJP of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai. MNS supremo urges people not to fall in a "political trap" He alleges that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday questioned the AIMIM-Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) alliance for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, alleging that the two parties could indirectly help the BJP by contesting separately instead of joining the INDIA bloc.Reacting to the formation of the 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha', Hussain Dalwai said the alliance raised suspicions about the parties' political intentions and questioned why they had chosen to form a separate front instead of becoming part of the opposition alliance."This gives rise to the suspicion that they intend to act as the BJP's team and help the party. People will not believe whatever these leaders say," he said.Earlier today, AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Azad announced their alliance, Samajik Parivartan Morcha, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with Azad being the candidate for chief minister.The two leaders made the announcement at a joint press conference in Lucknow, bringing together their parties ahead of the state polls. Azad said the coalition was open to other parties, including the Samajwadi Party and Congress, if they wanted to contest the elections in support of the alliance to prevent the BJP from returning to power in Uttar Pradesh, PTI reported.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: Delhi-based defence entrepreneur alleges fresh threat from gangster Rohit Godara, Rs 5 crore extortion demand
Article Text:
Gangster Rohit Godara (R) named in fresh Rs 5 crore extortion threat to Delhi businessman (L)

Luthra alleges repeated threats since 2024

NEW DELHI: A Delhi-based defence entrepreneur has alleged that gangster Rohit Godara demanded Rs 5 crore from him and issued a fresh death threat, prompting him to approach Delhi Police for protection.The businessman, who claims to have faced repeated extortion attempts and threats since 2024, has sought an investigation into the latest threat and the alleged involvement of the gangster.Sahil Luthra, founder and managing director of Vijayan Trishul Defence Solutions Private Limited, submitted a complaint to the Station House Officer (SHO) of Chanakyapuri police station on November 12.He alleged that he received the latest threat on November 11 at around 8 pm and attributed it to Godara.Luthra has sought immediate police protection and a detailed investigation into the alleged extortion demand and death threat. The complaint also refers to an earlier case registered at Chanakyapuri police station on October 17, 2025.In his complaint, Luthra alleged that he had been facing repeated threats and extortion attempts since 2024. He also claimed that he was being surveilled and that confidential information was being leaked, seeking a probe into these allegations.The businessman has urged Delhi Police to ensure his safety and investigate the alleged involvement of Godara and other persons.Police have received the latest complaint and are verifying its contents before taking further necessary action.Earlier, in June, Luthra had alleged a conspiracy to extort Rs 10 crore from him, claiming that he had received repeated threats through WhatsApp calls and chats from international gangs.He alleged that threatening calls and chats were received in August-September 2025 and again in June 2026.In August, Delhi's Patiala House court granted regular bail to Gurpinder Singh, accused in a case linked to the alleged extortion conspiracy.Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Animesh Kumar granted bail to Gurpinder Singh subject to furnishing a bail bond of Rs 50,000 with a surety in the like amount.While granting bail, the court said that although the allegations against the applicant were serious in nature, it could not be ignored that his custodial interrogation was not otherwise required.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Sahil Luthra, founder and managing director of Vijayan Trishul Defence Solutions Private Limited, submitted a complaint to the Station House Officer (SHO) of Chanakyapuri police station on November 12. He alleged that he received the latest threat on November 11 at around 8 pm and attributed it to Godara. The businessman has sought immediate police protection and a detailed investigation into the alleged extortion demand.

Article Title: Mumbai police order first eviction under Maharashtra Rent Control Act
Article Text:
City police have completed their first eviction under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, returning a flat to its owners.

MUMBAI: City police have decided their first eviction case under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999, and handed over "vacant and peaceful" possession of a Santacruz East flat to its owners, Prakash Digambar Deodhar and Prabha Prakash Deodhar.The owners alleged the occupants failed to vacate the flat at Jay Cooperative Housing Society on Nehru Road after a registered 36-month leave-and-licence agreement expired. Joint commissioner of police (law and order) Manojkumar Sharma said it was the first case brought by police under the new arrangement.After examining the applications, written statements, agreement and other documents, they rejected the tenants' request to contest the proceedings and allowed the owners' plea, an officer said.The tenants have been directed to pay compensation at twice the monthly licence fee from Sept 1 until possession was handed over.The state housing department had on July 31 appointed all 15 zonal deputy commissioners of police as competent authorities under the Act.The notification empowers deputy commissioners to hear applications, conduct inquiries, record evidence, issue eviction orders and direct police stations under their command to enforce them.At an April 10 review chaired by chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, govt data showed about 18,553 rent-related cases pending in Mumbai civil courts, many for years. Fadnavis directed the appointment of deputy commissioners as authorised officers and establishment of 100 special courts, including evening courts, to tackle the backlog.Residents seeking to recover homes after leave-and-licence agreements expire may apply to the relevant deputy commissioner with the necessary documents.Applications without a termination-date clause may be rejected, DCP Nimit Goyal said. "Residents seeking to recover homes after leave-and-licence agreements expire may apply to the relevant deputy commissioner with the necessary documents. Applications without a termination-date clause may be rejected," he added.Tenancy lawyer Divyakant Mehta said small causes courts could instead have been empowered to ensure uniformity and procedural expertise. He warned that orders could vary among the 15 officers unless a standard operating procedure was framed.Advocate Satyan Israni said the state's move is to bridge the gap in the execution of judicial orders.
Article Summary: City police have decided their first eviction case under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999. They handed over "vacant and peaceful" possession of a Santacruz East flat to its owners. Owners alleged occupants failed to vacate the flat after a registered 36-month leave-and-licence agreement expired.

Article Title: Not every insult attracts sec 299 of BNS: HC quashes FIR over FB post
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high ourt has quashed an FIR registered against social worker Mohammad Hisham Osmani over a Facebook post, holding that not every insult or objectionable statement necessarily attracts Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The court observed that section 299 applies only to an aggravated form of insult to religion or religious beliefs, accompanied by a deliberate and malicious intention to outrage the religious feelings of a particular class of citizens.Justice Sushil M. Ghodeswar passed the order on Nov 3, allowing Osmani’s criminal application seeking quashing of the FIR. The FIR was registered at Pundaliknagar police station on Feb 21, 2026, under section 299 of the BNS, which carries a punishment of up to three years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both.Osmani, a former city president of the Congress party, had resigned from the party in protest against the renaming of Aurangabad as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The FIR was lodged by Ashok More Patil for an offence said to have occurred between Feb 19 and 21. The FIR mentions that on the evening of Feb 19, a cultural programme was held in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti and telecast live on television.More alleged that on Feb 21, he saw a Facebook profile in the applicant's name on his mobile phone and found a post carrying sarcastic remarks in Hindi, using metaphors of donkeys and mujra against certain persons and their boss. He claimed it hurt his religious feelings.The HC had allowed a connected application filed by Vinod Narayan Patil as an intervenor. While representing Osmani, Adv SS Kazi submitted before the HC that the police registered the FIR without any inquiry and without calling Osmani, and also that he was unaware of it.Kazi submitted that after an objection was received over the post, a police officer asked Osmani to delete it at around 10 pm on Feb 21, about four hours after the FIR was registered, and that he deleted it immediately.Kazi, appearing for the applicant, read out section 299 and argued that no offence under it was made out. Assistant public prosecutor for the state and complainant’s advocate opposed the petition, submitting that the investigation was almost complete and the charge sheet was being prepared.Witness statements showed that the post was found on the Facebook account maintained by the applicant.After going through the FIR and the statements recorded by the investigating officer, the high court said that even if the post was taken at face value, it did not disclose any specific insult to the religion or religious beliefs of any particular class of citizens.“Mere use of insulting or abusive expressions against certain persons, without satisfying the aforesaid essential ingredients, would not constitute an offence under section 299,” it observed.The HC concluded that to prevent abuse of the process of the court and secure the ends of justice, it quashed the FIR and consequential proceedings, if any, to the extent of the applicant.
Article Summary: Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high ourt has quashed an FIR registered against social worker Mohammad Hisham Osmani over a Facebook post. The FIR was lodged by Ashok More Patil for an offence said to have occurred between Feb 19 and 21.

Article Title: 4 govt directors help BJP-led group win Kolhapur's Gokul polls; another form of vote and election chori, says Congress
Article Text:
Maharashtra’s BJP-led Mahayuti alliance secured victory in the Gokul Dairy chief election held recently





KOLHAPUR: Maharashtra ’s governing BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched Tuesday a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief, riding on the support of four new govt nominees.Mahayuti candidate, ex-NCP MLA Rajesh Patil, was elected chief after securing 16 votes, three more than his Samavichari rival Patil Chuyekar’s 13.Gokul has a 25-member board of directors, for which elections were held last month. Mahayuti had won 12 posts and Samavichari 13. Neither had the quorum of 14 required for the chief’s election.Mahayuti govt had last week promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large cooperatives, four with voting rights.This drew flak from the opposition, which accused govt of attempting to grab Gokul, the state’s largest milk co-operative. Congress LS leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged “adulteration” of the mandate. A Samavichari plea in Bombay HC against the ordinance was rejected Monday.“We have nominated individuals with experience. If one is a gynaecologist, what’s wrong? When the country’s leader of opposition feels the need to intervene in a milk union election, a gynaecologist is just a common citizen,” CM Devendra Fadnavis said on Tuesday.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal denounced the outcome as “another form of vote and election chori”.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief. Rajesh Patil, ex-NCP MLA, was elected chief after securing 16 votes.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Sad day for democracy, if peaceful protesters charged with criminal offence: HC
Article Text:
Nagpur:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





The Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court said it would be a “sad day for democracy” if criminal cases are filed against peaceful protesters and quashed an FIR against a Chandrapur man, who led an agitation for repair of a battered road. Justice MW Chandwani held the prosecution of 26-year-old Nishkarsh Nimgade was an abuse of the process of law.Citing a Supreme Court ruling, Justice Chandwani said, “It is a settled law that prosecutions must not be launched to stifle agitations that are part of democratic process as long as protesters don’t take the law into their own hands or indulge in violence or damage public or private property.”The court noted Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees the right to assemble peacefully and without arms. On limits to that right, Justice Chandwani said, “While reasonable restrictions could always be imposed on exercising this fundamental right, it must not be diluted or stifled on vague charges bereft of essential ingredients to constitute offences under law.”According to the prosecution, a pickup vehicle hit an electricity pole and overturned near Nandgaon on Jan 21, leaving at least one person critically injured.A crowd gathered at the spot and demanded action against PWD officials and the contractor for poor quality of the road. Mul police named a Nimgade in an FIR for wrongful restraint, unlawful assembly and other offences.The court said the chargesheet did not specify who obstructed traffic and no passerby’s statement was recorded. It noted the accused’s name did not figure in the portion of the FIR alleging obstruction, and that he was found later with those agitating, which could not be termed an offence. No prohibitory order was on record to attract Section 135 of Maharashtra Police Act, the court said.The court quashed the FIR, the chargesheet and the case pending before the judicial magistrate first class at Mul, only in respect of Nimgade.
Article Summary: Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court said it would be a “sad day for democracy’ if criminal cases are filed against peaceful protesters. Justice MW Chandwani held the prosecution of 26-year-old Nishkarsh Nimgade was an abuse of the process of law.

A 21-year-old driver was stabbed multiple times and attacked with a liquor bottle and a stick by four men in Rajiv Nagar on Wednesday evening.The incident occurred near Shiv Durga Temple within the limits of MIDC police station. Satyendra claimed he met a woman, whom he considers his sister, on Bhai Dooj, but this angered his ex-girlfriend’s husband.As per Satyendra, the key accused called him to a spot opposite Rajiv Nagar on the pretext of a meeting related to his wife. Between 7.35 pm and 8.10 pm on Wednesday, the accused, along with three others — Jackie Singh, Indrajit Yadav and Sunny Paswan — arrived in two cars.An argument broke out. The key suspect then allegedly stabbed Satyendra on the right side of the chest, back and below the waist with a knife. The others hit him on the head with a liquor bottle and a stick. The attackers then fled the scene.Satyendra is undergoing treatment at a private hospital. MIDC police have registered an offence for an attempt to murder. Investigation is underway.

Article Title: Morshi police seize Rs35 lakh gutkha smuggled from MP
Article Text:
Amravati:





Gutkha and scented tobacco products worth about Rs35 lakh being smuggled into Maharashtra from Madhya Pradesh were seized during nakabandi at Morshi. The driver of a four-wheeler was arrested, while a case has been registered against three others.Assistant police inspector Nilesh Deshmukh of Special Inspector General of Police Office (Amravati Range) had received information on Monday that a large stock of gutkha was being brought into Amravati district. Police laid a trap on Monday under the guidance of Morshi police station in-charge Rahul Athawale.Police stopped the vehicle and recovered scented tobacco and gutkha. The driver admitted that the gutkha was brought from Pandhurna (MP) and was to be unloaded at godowns at Badnera and Amravati, said police. On the complaint of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) officer Ghansham Dande, a case has been registered against four persons.
Article Summary: Police laid a trap on Monday under the guidance of Morshi police station in- charge Rahul Athawale. The driver admitted that the gutkha was brought from Pandhurna (MP) and was to be unloaded at godowns at Badnera and Amravati, said police.

Former MP and BJP state vice-president Sujay Vikhe Patil was elected unopposed as chairperson of the Ahilyanagar District Central Cooperative Bank on Thursday, following a rare alliance between political rivals — guardian and water resources minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and former revenue minister Balasaheb Thorat.Ranjitsinh Deshmukh was elected unopposed as vice-chairperson. Backed by 20 of the 21 directors, including independents and the Ram Shinde faction, Vikhe’s selection followed his panel’s victory in 17 of the 21 seats, out of which 10 were won unopposed. Playing a key coordinating role in bringing the opposing factions together, Vikhe Patil celebrated with supporters after taking charge.“We all will work with cohesion for the welfare of the bank, farmers and industries. We will function under the directions of senior leaders in the district and serve in the best interest of the bank’s owners i.e. the farmers,” Vikhe Patil told the reporters.On the eve of the election, Sangamner director Ranjitsinh Deshmukh met Lok Sabha MP Nilesh Lanke at Supa rest house, sparking speculation. Defending the alliance, Thorat said farmers’ welfare outweighed politics amid drought conditions.“The district bank belongs to the common man and must survive.Given the drought-like situation, we kept politics aside and came together to work for farmers,” Thorat said.Meanwhile, Lanke, the lone opposition director who skipped the election process and signed the attendance register after arriving late, vowed to act as a strict watchdog. Declining to comment on internal backing, he said that the majority holds the right to decide.“I am alone in the opposition in the bank. I am the chowkidaar (watchman). I will keep a strict vigil and discharge this duty honestly,” Lanke said, demanding large-scale crop loans at low interest rates. If only my farmer survives will the sugar industry survive,” he added.
Article Summary: Former MP and BJP state vice-president Sujay Vikhe Patil was elected unopposed as chairperson of the Ahilyanagar District Central Cooperative Bank on Thursday. He was backed by 20 of the 21 directors, including independents and the Ram Shinde faction. Former revenue minister Balasaheb Thorat was elected as vice- chairperson.

Article Title: SIT names ex-Chennai police commissioner A Arun, 6 others in Veeramani POCSO case
Article Text:
Ex-Chennai police chief A Arun named accused in POCSO case against Gem Granites founder

SIT files 720-page chargesheet

SIT registers seven fresh cases





CHENNAI: Former Chennai police commissioner A Arun and six other police personnel have been named as accused in a case linked to alleged lapses in the investigation of a POCSO complaint against Gem Granites founder R Veeramani.The development comes as the Special Investigation Team (SIT) filed its first chargesheet against Veeramani and two of his drivers for the alleged sexual abuse of a 14-year-old Dalit girl.Police sources said the seven officers, including former Anti-Vice Squad assistant commissioner M A Yasmin, have been named in the first FIR registered by the SIT.They are accused of failing to conduct a proper inquiry into the original complaint, which resulted in a closure report being filed before a special court earlier this year.Separately, the SIT filed its first chargesheet against Veeramani and his two car drivers, Parthiban and Babu, in connection with the alleged sexual abuse of the minor girl.The 720-page final report, which cites 40 witnesses, was submitted before the Special Court for exclusive trial of cases under the POCSO Act at the High Court campus on November 11.The chargesheet was filed within 46 days of the case being registered on September 27.According to investigators, Veeramani, the prime accused, sexually abused the minor girl. His drivers have been accused of transporting the survivor to and dropping her at his residence despite allegedly knowing about the offence.The three accused have been charged under relevant provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.The SIT was constituted on September 24 by the Director General of Police (DGP), under the supervision of the Greater Chennai Police Commissioner, to investigate the original case and related matters.Following its formation, seven fresh cases involving nine minor survivors were registered based on complaints filed by the victims or their mothers.Eight associates of Veeramani have also been arrested in connection with the network. Meanwhile, the SIT is continuing its parallel investigation into the seven police officials named in the FIR.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Ex-Chennai police chief A Arun named accused in POCSO case against Gem Granites founder R Veeramani. Former Anti-Vice Squad assistant commissioner M A Yasmin also named in the first FIR registered by the SIT. The development comes as the Special Investigation Team (SIT) filed its first chargesheet against VeerAmani and two of his drivers.

A special court for corruption cases in the city has sent former MLA Muthukumaran, arrested in connection with the ₹100 crore private schools cheating case, to five days of police custody.Special judge L S Sathiyamurthy passed the order on the ground that the CCB has to ascertain the actual sum of the amount received by A1 (B T Arasakumar) and A2 ( Muthukumar ) for A5 (Anbil Mahesh), from the statements of accounts and records collected in the investigation.“Therefore, A2 has to be interrogated in this regard is also one of the reasons stated by the CCB. The accused had used various places to store the amount and also availed the services of middlemen for logistic purposes. The ultimate destination of the monies and properties purchased by using it are also important and to be investigated. Therefore, this court is of the view that the reasons are valid and sustainable,” the court said.Granting custody of the accused, the court added that the investigating officer shall not subject the accused to any threat, inducement, coercion, physical assault, mental harassment or third-degree methods during the course of custodial interrogations.The court also allowed advocate of the accused to remain present within the line of sight of the interrogation. “But shall be positioned at a distance without being within hearing distance. Every day at 5 pm the advocate and the respondent can meet for 10 minutes,” the court said.
Article Summary: Muthukumaran was arrested in connection with the ₹100 crore private schools cheating case. Special judge L S Sathiyamurthy passed the order on the ground that the CCB has to ascertain the actual sum of the amount received by the accused.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment
Article Text:
Cop suspended over woman’s plaint of house trespass, sexual harassment





Tuticorin: A special branch head constable of Tharuvaikulam police station in Tuticorin district has been placed under suspension after a woman accused him of trespassing into her house and making obscene and sexually suggestive gestures while purportedly enquiring about her brother.A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother, who was reportedly involved in a matrimonial dispute. On Nov 6, when she was alone at home, the constable entered the premises and behaved in an obscene manner, making sexually suggestive gestures and stating that he had come specifically to see and speak with her, she said.The complainant alleged that when she questioned his repeated visits and raised an alarm, the constable fled. She immediately alerted police and later lodged a formal complaint. Subsequently, DSP M Sundarapandiyan conducted an inquiry with both the complainant and the accused. Based on the findings, police registered a case for house-trespass, sexual harassment and action intended to insult the modesty of a woman under BNS, and Section 4 (harassment of women) of Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.Police said a notice was served on the accused, and departmental action also initiated. Selvin Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.
Article Summary: A case was registered against Selvin Raja, 37, based on a complaint from the victim. The woman alleged that Raja visited her residence on Oct 27 and Nov 2 under the pretext of inquiring about her brother. Raja was placed under suspension on Nov 7, and further investigation was underway.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: Accident accused arrested after 16 years in hiding

Pattanakkad Police in Alappuzha has arrested a man who went absconding after being involved in a 2010 road accident that killed two people.Rajeesh Omanakuttan, 43, of Thundiyilkadavu, Nattakam, Kottayam, was caught on Thanneermukkam Bund Road and handed over to Alappuzha South police earlier this week.The accident happened at Thumboli, Alappuzha South. The police said the vehicle driven by Omanakuttan hit and killed Shanmughan and Tracy. He then abandoned the vehicle and went into hiding in Tamil Nadu under a false identity.A special team under Cherthala DSP Manjulal was formed after district police chief Vishnu Pradeep T K received a tip-off that Omanakuttan was back in Keralam.Tracking him to Pattanakkad limits, the team followed him as he allegedly tried to flee back to Tamil Nadu via Vagamon and Kumily. He turned back after the police there tightened border checks. The police finally intercepted him after a 300-km chase at Thanneermukkam Bund Road while he was trying to escape via the Kallara-Vechoor road.
Article Summary: Rajeesh Omanakuttan, 43, of Thundiyilkadavu, Nattakam, Kottayam, was caught on Thanneermukkam Bund Road and handed over to Alappuzha South police earlier this week.
